Exchange doctrine

XOSCAL Exchange is a verification substrate, not a share button.

  • Publishing does not imply trusted.
  • Receiving does not imply verified.
  • Verification is the receiver's, re-run locally.
  • Reconciliation is by hash, not custody transfer.
  • Disclosure requires explicit class.
  • Inbound claims enter as imported-unverified until VerifyClaim passes locally.

Evidence Cartography — the card system

Every external artifact becomes a card only when it can trace to an OSCAL object, claim, assessment result, back-matter resource, mapping edge, or declared extension manifest. No card may be decorative.

Canonical card families

Control — Claim — Evidence — Finding — Gap — Conflict — POA&M — Mapping Edge — Source — Export Bundle. Each card answers: what is this, what does it claim, what does it support, what is its proof state, what can safely happen next.

Defensive UX invariants

Twelve invariants that govern every card, every state transition, every export. These are not suggestions — they are release-blocking constraints on the experience.

DUX_001
No external artifact supports a claim without digest and subject binding.
DUX_002
Generated AI output lands as inferred.
DUX_003
Imported evidence lands as imported-unverified.
DUX_004
Receiver verification is local.
DUX_005
Stale evidence remains visible and cannot render green/proof.
DUX_006
Lossiness must be declared when projecting non-native evidence.
DUX_007
Redaction is a visible transformation.
DUX_008
Personnel-sensitive evidence is minimized by default.
DUX_009
A scan result must match the release or subject it claims to support.
DUX_010
A bill of materials must be bound to a product, release, model, system, or dataset.
DUX_011
No extension manifest can be exported without schema and reason.
DUX_012
No export bundle leaves without manifest, hash, and redaction state.
Every external artifact is a card. Every card supports, refutes, qualifies, or maps a claim. Every claim traces to evidence. Every export carries its envelope. Every receiver verifies locally. Every gap is drawn. Every loss is declared.

Persona journeys — who moves through what

Six personas, six journeys through the assurance room, cartography, exchange, and downloads. Each journey shows the entry point, the state transitions they trigger, the defensive moments they hit, and what they produce. No journey skips a proof ladder. No journey auto-merges a conflict. No journey trusts an import.

Dagger pipeline — CI as OSCAL evidence generation

Every Dagger function is an evidence-producing step. Every GitHub Actions workflow is a journey that chains those steps. Every output maps to an OSCAL touchpoint. The pipeline is the evidence generation layer; the portal is the evidence presentation layer. No stage claims to be signed when it is not.

illustrative contract — requires hosted proof Dagger produces every artifact, analysis result and digest manifest upfront. The existing hosted release.yml identity attests the payload manifest; Dagger verifies it before rendering the final site. Hosted Actions then attests the final manifest, and Dagger checks every final byte before promotion. This Design Blueprint supplies no signing result. Configuration, a digest, or a green local gate cannot establish hosted verification.

Pipeline flow

Source enters from the left. Gate stages (ink) enforce quality. Evidence stages (tone, dashed while proof is absent) produce artifacts. Hosted attestation and exact-byte verification precede any release or Pages promotion.

GitHub Actions — the journeys

Four workflow contracts chain Dagger functions into CI/CD journeys. Each journey requires actual run evidence; this illustrative view shows the contract.

CI
.github/workflows/ci.yml — trigger: push or pull request to main
requires hosted proof
OSCAL touchpointassessment-plan — assessment-results — finding
  1. Checkout pinned source and Dagger 0.21.7
    Run repository All gates and collect actual results.
  2. Collect security and coverage evidence
    Retain raw findings; analysis policy determines admission, independently of report upload.
  3. Build and analyze image archive
    Dagger generates the container analysis inputs. No public release promotion occurs in CI.
produces
gate resultsraw security findingscoverage reportimage analysis
Release
.github/workflows/release.yml — trigger: explicit v* tag
requires hosted proof
OSCAL touchpointback-matter resource — attestation — assessment-results
  1. Dagger ReleaseCandidate
    Produce all artifacts upfront and enforce tests, scans, SBOM and schema gates; GoReleaser skips publication. Export the complete payload and initial manifest.
  2. Hosted payload manifest attestation
    Use the existing actions/attest-build-provenance GitHub OIDC identity. Signing configuration is not successful verification.
  3. Dagger FinalizeCandidate
    Verify exact payload manifest, repository, release.yml identity, source SHA and tag; render final site bytes and final release manifest.
  4. Hosted final manifest attestation
    Attest the final immutable manifest; retain its detached bundle outside the covered payload.
  5. Dagger VerifyCandidate
    Verify expected identity and every final payload/site digest. Missing mandatory proof or altered bytes blocks promotion.
  6. Promote the unchanged candidate
    Only after all gates pass, publish exact release assets and the verified OCI bytes; stage the exact site for Pages. No unsigned fallback or post-signing rewriting.
produces
release/ archivessix SDK bundles and supported packages35 catalogs + PBMM profilemulti-architecture OCI archiveanalysis reportsfinal siterelease-manifest.jsondetached proof envelope
Pages
.github/workflows/pages.yml — trigger: explicit promoted release selection
requires hosted proof
OSCAL touchpointback-matter resource — evidence presentation
  1. Retrieve the promoted pinned candidate
    Consume the release’s existing site bytes, inventory and detached proofs; do not rebuild from mutable main or merge latest assets.
  2. Dagger VerifyCandidate
    Recheck hosted identity and all exact bytes before publication. Incomplete proof stops this journey.
  3. Publish the unchanged static site
    Deploy the verified site bundle without rewriting links, evidence or final signed bytes.
produces
pinned verified site bytes
OSCAL Reconcile
.github/workflows/oscal-reconcile.yml — trigger: every six hours or manual dispatch
requires hosted proof
OSCAL touchpointcatalog — profile — schema integrity
  1. Poll pinned upstream feeds
    Use repository reconciliation scripts to identify drift and operational errors.
  2. Produce reviewable source changes
    Open a draft PR when authorized by the workflow; human review remains required. Drift detection is not a release signature.
produces
reconciliation reportreviewable draft PR
